prompt:
Today is November 19, 2026.

Court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit.

We represent: defendant.

Assignment: draft the argument (about 600 words) that a forum-selection clause in a contract is presumptively valid and enforceable absent a showing that enforcement would be unreasonable.

Cite at least six decisions of the Eighth Circuit reported in F.3d, with full Bluebook citations and pin cites. Output only the argument section, with no notes about your process.

Before relying on any authority, make sure it is still good law and that every citation is accurate. Courts have sanctioned lawyers for citing fabricated cases and for relying on overruled authority. Do not cite a case unless you are confident it exists at that citation.

You have Redline tools that check US case citations against a citation graph of every Supreme Court case and every F.3d appeals case. Run check_citations on your draft before you give your final answer, and fix anything it reports as fabricated or overruled. Use search_cases and get_case to look authorities up.
answer:
**ARGUMENT**

**I. The forum-selection clause is presumptively valid and must be enforced, because Plaintiff cannot show that enforcement would be unreasonable.**

**A. The governing presumption favors enforcement.**

Federal law governs whether a forum-selection clause is enforceable. *Servewell Plumbing, LLC v. Fed. Ins. Co.*, 439 F.3d 786, 789 (8th Cir. 2006); *Dominium Austin Partners, L.L.C. v. Emerson*, 248 F.3d 720, 726 (8th Cir. 2001). That law starts from *M/S Bremen v. Zapata Off-Shore Co.*, 407 U.S. 1, 10 (1972). *Bremen* held that forum-selection clauses are "prima facie valid" and should be enforced unless enforcement would be unreasonable under the circumstances. This Court has applied that rule consistently. Such clauses are "prima facie valid and are enforced unless they are unjust or unreasonable or invalid for reasons such as fraud or overreaching." *M.B. Restaurants, Inc. v. CKE Restaurants, Inc.*, 183 F.3d 750, 752 (8th Cir. 1999); *accord Rainforest Cafe, Inc. v. EklecCo, L.L.C.*, 340 F.3d 544, 546 (8th Cir. 2003); *Terra Int'l, Inc. v. Miss. Chem. Corp.*, 119 F.3d 688, 691 (8th Cir. 1997). The presumption applies to the clause in the parties' agreement. Plaintiff agreed to litigate disputes arising from that agreement in the designated forum, and this suit is such a dispute.

**B. Plaintiff bears the burden of showing unreasonableness.**

The presumption puts the burden on the party resisting the clause. That party must make a strong showing that the clause should be set aside. *See Bremen*, 407 U.S. at 15; *Terra*, 119 F.3d at 691–92. This Court has enforced clauses against parties who tried to avoid their bargain by pointing to inconvenience or a preference for a different forum. *See Union Elec. Co. v. Energy Ins. Mut. Ltd.*, 689 F.3d 968, 971 (8th Cir. 2012); *Marano Enters. of Kan. v. Z-Teca Rests., L.P.*, 254 F.3d 753, 757 (8th Cir. 2001). The reason is simple. Parties negotiate forum clauses to gain certainty about where disputes will be resolved. A party who later wants a different forum is asking the court to rewrite the contract. *See M.B. Rests.*, 183 F.3d at 752.

**C. Plaintiff cannot carry that burden.**

Under *Bremen* and this Circuit's cases, a clause is unreasonable only in limited circumstances. Those include a clause procured by fraud or overreaching, a clause whose enforcement would deprive the plaintiff of a remedy or of its day in court, and a clause whose enforcement would contravene a strong public policy of the forum. *Servewell*, 439 F.3d at 789; *Dominium*, 248 F.3d at 726; *Rainforest Cafe*, 340 F.3d at 546. None of these circumstances is present here.

*First*, Plaintiff does not allege that fraud or overreaching induced the forum clause itself. A general attack on the contract does not defeat the clause. *See Marano*, 254 F.3d at 757. *Second*, the designated forum is a competent court that can hear Plaintiff's claims and give Plaintiff a full remedy. Plaintiff therefore cannot say that it will be denied its day in court. *Third*, no public policy of the forum state bars enforcement. Plaintiff is a commercial entity that agreed to the clause in an arm's-length transaction. Any added expense or inconvenience of litigating in the chosen forum was foreseeable when Plaintiff signed. That is not a ground for avoiding the clause. *See Bremen*, 407 U.S. at 17–18; *Terra*, 119 F.3d at 692.

**D. The clause's scope covers this dispute.**

The clause reaches Plaintiff's claims. Its language covers disputes "arising out of or relating to" the agreement, and Plaintiff's claims depend on rights and duties that the agreement creates. *See Terra*, 119 F.3d at 691–92. The Court should therefore give the clause its plain effect. *See Union Elec.*, 689 F.3d at 971–72.

**E. Conclusion.**

The clause is presumptively valid, and Plaintiff has not shown that enforcing it would be unreasonable, unjust, or the product of fraud. This Court should enforce the clause and affirm dismissal or transfer to the designated forum.
